overview: White pins or threatens the f6 knight with Bg5 and then plays e3, Nbd2, c3 and Bd3 (or c4) in a flexible pyramid-like set-up. Black usually answers 3...e6 and ...c5 or ...Nbd7, or 3...Ne4 (Gossip Variation) trading the bishop. White's plans are simple: build a solid centre, castle, and aim for e4 or a kingside initiative. It is an easy-to-learn system against 1...d5 that is playable against most Black set-ups.

white_ideas.idea: e3, Nbd2, c3 and Bd3, a solid pyramid set-up against any defence
Prepare e4 or a kingside attack with Ne5, Qf3 and h4 in some lines
Trade on f6 to damage Black's pawns or take the bishop pair against ...Ne4

black_ideas.idea: ...e6, ...c5 and ...Nc6 to challenge the d4 pawn
...Ne4 to trade the bishop and relieve the pin (Gossip Variation)

typical_structures.structure: White pyramid d4/e3/c3 against ...e6/...c5, flexible centre tension

character.notes: Solid structure for White like the London and Colle; Black can create tactics with ...Ne4 or ...c5 but the usual game is steady.

gambit.notes: No material is given in main lines.

structure.notes: Centre in tension, White keeps c4 or e4 in reserve, so Flexible like the London.

approach.notes: A system set-up playable against nearly any defence to the queen's pawn.

level.notes: Clear plans, little to memorise, like the London and Colle.

sublines_that_differ.name: Gossip Variation
sublines_that_differ.how: Black trades the bishop and plays for easy equality, a more open game.

sublines_that_differ.name: Grünfeld Variation
sublines_that_differ.how: Black sets up a fianchetto and avoids ...e6, leading to a London-like game.
